findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed one dead, and one live fly during today’s spot check. Obtain pest control provider by next routine inspection. Pest control devices (such as fly strips) may be purchased to manage pests, just ensure they are away from food storage.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) items were out of proper cold holding temperature. The ambient temperature of the open air cooler was initially observed at 51F, and went down to 41F (no indication of defrost on cooler). As a result, multiple TCS items were probed for internal temperatures:
1) Three cheeseburgers were probed at temperatures of 48(X2) and 45F.
2) Three Chobani yogurts were probed at 48(X2) and 47F.
3) Two steak and jalapeno burritos were probed at 49 and 51F.
4) Two beef and bean burritos were probed at 48 and 46F.
5) One country fried chicken was probed at 47F.
6) One smoked ham and turkey club was probed at 48F.
7) Two smoked ham and swiss sandwiches were both probed at 48F. 
8) Two egg and sausage burritos were probed at 50 and 51F.
9) One Italian wrap was probed at 48F.
10) One chicken and Ceasar wrap was probed at 47F.
11) One buffalo chicken wrap was probed at 47F.
12) Two packaged of creamer in the dispenser were also observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. Creamers were voluntarily discarded.

Three items not listed in numbers 1-11 were probed from the open air cooler and had internal temperatures below 41F. CORRECTED- due to all of the previously mentioned foods being prepackaged, they had to be discarded to be probed. The inspector notified the person in charge (PIC) of the need to probe and discard foods due to high temperature readings. The PIC stated they check cooler temperatures at the end of the shift daily. Inspector encourages use of a daily temperature log to monitor temperatures for cold holding units. Ensure TCS foods are kept at or below 41F to prevent the growth of microorganisms that may cause foodborne-illnesses.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the creamers at the dispenser to not contain date marking. The PIC stated they were not certain when they were last refilled, but it is likely that it has been over seven days. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded creamers. Ensure TCS foods that require opening are marked with the date they are opened, and used or discarded within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple chemicals (washer fluid, glass cleaner, and exhaust fluid) being stored over drinks in the back storage. Chemicals should be stored under or away from food products to prevent potential contamination of foods. Inspector will return on 10/14/25 to ensure chemicals are stored below or away from foods.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Multiple flies (both dead and live) were observed throughout the facility. Flies were observed near the front register, soda machines, and on the shelving of the open air cooler. The PIC was unsure of who the facility uses for pest control. Flies pose a risk of contaminating food sources. If the facility uses a pest control operator, reach out to schedule an appointment, or obtain pest control devices. If there is no Pest Control Operator, ensure one is obtained. Inspector will return on 10/23/25 to check how the flies are being managed.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed single service cups stored on the ground. Single service articles should be stored at least 6 inches above the ground to protect food contacts surfaces from contamination, and also prevent the attraction of pests. Ensure all single service items are stored on facilities’ shelving.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation of debris: 
1) Mold is growing and accumulating on the sides and back of the self-dispensing soda machines.
2) Mold was observed along the individual line shelving of the drink coolers. 
Clean and sanitize nonfood contact surfaces at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of mold, or other contaminants. Items may be wiped with a clean sanitizer cloth, power washed, or washed in the facility’s three compartment sink.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed water pooling on the floor behind the soda machines. The source of the leak appeared to be a carbonator below the soda machines. Contact supplier to service the connection line to prevent leakage. Pooling water may attract pest and allow for the growth and harborage of microorganisms that thrive in high levels of water activity.
findings.citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two wet mops on the floor. Discussion between the PIC and inspector occurred regarding storage of mops. Mops should be stored in a position that allows air drying to occur. Mops that are unable to air dry harbor bacteria that feed on the fats broken down by soaps and detergents. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows for air drying in the future.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a square hold about 10”x10” to the right of the mop sink, as well as a circular hole in the wall to the right of the soda machines in the back. The hole next to the mop sink allows for access to water shut off. Exposed drywall or wood should be painted or sealed to prevent the entry of water. Cover circular opening, and obtain a door or seal/ paint the drywall next to the mop sink. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair. Ensure repairs are made with nonabsorbent materials; smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of soda splash and debris in the wall behind and floor below the soda boxes. This sugar rich debris attracts and helps to harbor pests (see violation #38). Facility should clean at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The soda nozzles and the dispenser parts of the soda machine were observed to still have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- The operators cleaned the dispensers and the nozzles during the inspection today. It was discussed with the operators to make sure that the dispensers and the nozzles are being cleaned and scrubbed daily. It was recommended to have a second set of nozzles to allow for more time for cleaning or to get clear nozzles which allow any soil accumulation to be seen better. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

Ensure that the nozzles and the dispenser parts of the soda machine are cleaned. A follow up is scheduled for 5/29/2025 to ensure that the nozzles and dispenser parts of the machine have been cleaned.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall a concentration of 150-400ppm per manufacturer’s label. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Package of raw bacon was observed above bottled beverages in the reachin section of the cooler. Labeling for location of raw shell eggs and bacon were observed to be above bottled beverages as the permanent location. PIC was advised raw foods must be stored below ready to eat foods. Package of bacon was moved to bottom shelf of open air cooler to allow for proper storage. Ensure raw bacon and eggs are not stored above bottled beverages or other ready to eat foods available for purchase. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 (REPEAT) Mixing wand of the F'real machine was soiled with buildup of dried on food splash. The area just above the mixing cup was also soiled with stuck on food splash. Ensure the mixing wand and surfaces around it that accumulate food splash are cleaned and sanitized at least up to every 4hrs (not more than 6hrs) after continuous use. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat sanitizer was not dispensing at proper concentration. Product observed around 100ppm, and the effective concentration is 150-400ppm. PIC was advised to call for service and get the dispenser repaired. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Soda nozzles were observed with varying amounts of mold buildup. Ensure nozzles and area on the machine where they attach are getting properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized as needed to eliminate buildup.
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 PIC indicated the 3 part sink has not been used for manual ware washing, which means food contact surfaces that need to be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized were not being properly cleaned and sanitized between uses. PIC was advised the 3 part sink is to be setup and used for proper manual ware washing moving forward. 
Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.
Items that need to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized include, but are not necessarily limited to, the containers and dispensing components of the cappuccino machine and soda nozzles.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle of Purell sanitizer had a blue liquid inside that was thought to be window cleaner. Another spray bottle that was labeled as DG window cleaner had a light pink liquid inside. The Purell bottle was for sure improperly labeled. Both solutions were discarded at the time of inspection. Proper labeling of chemicals was discussed.  
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site (bleach solution, etc.) shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Shrink wrapped packages of bottled water were observed on shelving and the ground on display outside the main entrance. PIC was advised bottled water is to be displayed and stored within the building. PIC stated this is common practice for stores in the area. PIC was advised this is a bad practice and needs to cease. Shrink wrapped packages of bottled water are just like any other food item and must be stored properly to protect product from potential contamination.
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Single use packets of ketchup, salt, and pepper were stored under the old handsink in the front service area. A leak occurred at some point and the packets were exposed to moisture and general splash. Packaging was soiled, and all packets were discarded in the trash during inspection. 
Food, single service, and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available to be used during hours of operation. A sanitizer solution should always be prepared and available for use.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-501.14 (REPEAT) Three part sink was soiled, especially the third basin and clean drain board. Three part sink and drain board were cleaned during the inspection
The compartments of sinks, basins, or other receptacles used for washing and rinsing equipment and utensils shall be cleaned: (A) before use, (B) throughout the day at a frequency necessary to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils and to ensure that the equipment performs its intended function; and (C) if used, at least every 24 hours.
